policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 24:6 renders 'them that seek after him': a plural participle governing a 3ms object, which is exactly the qere דֹּרְשָׁיו (plural participle + 3ms suffix). The ketiv דרשו reads as a singular participle with suffix ('his seeker', dorsho) or a finite verb without the object suffix; the ASV's explicit plural 'them that seek' and expressed object 'him' match neither. Wording decides for the qere.
